sections.history: Thiruchotruthurai stands on the southern bank of the Kaveri, some 7 km from Thiruvaiyaru and about 14 km from Thanjavur. Its lord was praised in the Tevaram by Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar, so the temple is counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. The oldest parts of the present masonry belong to the Chola period of the ninth century, and building went on in stages until the time of the Thanjavur Nayaks in the sixteenth century. The village name itself carries the temple's story: choru is the Tamil word for cooked rice, and thurai a riverside landing, so the name remembers a ghat where food was given.
sections.architecture: Walls pierced by four gopurams enclose the temple, and the Chola core around the sanctum is wrapped in later halls and corridors. The goddess, worshipped here as Annapoorani, the giver of food, and also as Oppilambikai, the one without equal, has her own shrine within the complex. Restoration work has been under way in recent years, so parts of the outer enclosure may be screened off when you visit.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of a terrible famine, when a devotee named Arulalar, unable to bear the suffering around him, resolved to give up his life before the lord. Shiva answered with rain, and with an akshaya patram, a vessel that could never be emptied, from which all the hungry were fed. So the lord came to be called Chotruthurainathar, and in Sanskrit Odhanavaneswarar, both names speaking of food given freely to all who came.
sections.festivals: In the Saptha Sthanam festival of Chithirai (April–May), the procession comes to Thiruchotruthurai after Thirupazhanam. Tradition holds that the food for Nandi's wedding feast was sent from here, and the temple still sends food for the yearly celebration of Nandi's wedding. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham are observed as well. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: This is a temple of food and generosity, and it is natural here to give thanks for the meal on one's own table. Pass through the gopurams to the sanctum, then go on to the goddess Annapoorani. The village is quiet and close to the river, and it joins easily with Thirupazhanam and Thiruvedhikudi on the same morning.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but strictly prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruchotruthurai lies on the southern side of the Kaveri, about 7 km from Thiruvaiyaru and 14 km from Thanjavur, and is reached by local bus, auto or taxi from either town. Thanjavur is the nearest major railway station, and Tiruchirappalli International Airport, roughly 65 km away, is the nearest airport.
